title: Sunrise rollout slate and signal annotations (2026-08) - WIP
summary: Working draft: phased 'sunrise' rollout plan with annotated telemetry signals and a compact release-notes template. Focused on low-latency features and regional warmups; includes preflight gates, mitigation playbook, and post-rollout observations to capture for follow-up evals.
body:
Context and intent:
This doc is a working slate for a low-risk morning ("sunrise") rollout pattern targeted at low-latency model tweaks and routing policy updates. Goal: get a small, measurable production exposure window early in the customer day to verify tail-latency improvements while preserving capacity headroom for rollback and recovery.

Why 'sunrise'?
- Early-day traffic in our largest US-west customers tends to be less spiky; easier signal-to-noise.
- Allows same-day remediation by US eng teams.
- Short, controlled ramp reduces blast radius while still exercising global routing.

High-level timeline (example window):
- T-72h: Internal readiness review (sigs: infra, SRE, observability, product-owner)
- T-48h: Lock release notes draft and schedule canary lanes
- T-24h: Preflight dry run in staging with traffic replay (check KV cache warmup and batching profiles)
- T-4h: Quiet window request to platform (throttle non-essential jobs + background maintenance)
- T-1h: Canary lane 1 (1% traffic) - 20 minutes steady-state, metrics snapshot
- T0: Ramp to Canary lane 2 (5% traffic) - 30 minutes, validate tail p95/p99 and error rates
- T+1h: If green, ramp to regional warmup (20% in US-west OR early-morning regions) + regression checks
- T+3h: Hold and review final telemetry; decide full rollout or rollback

Preflight checklist (must be green before T-4h):
- Release artifacts built and checksum verified (SHA256)
- Model binary / config pinned and available on artifact storage
- Infra capacity verified for maximum warmup ramp (reserve 30% headroom)
- Observability: dashboard snapshots created and shared link in #release-ops
- Alerting: short-lived alerts added for these checks (channel: #sentry-release, severity: P2)
- Canary lanes defined in routing policy with automatic rollback on threshold breach
- Canary traffic generator config validated in staging (traffic mix matches prod-percentiles)
- Rollback playbook published and assigned to oncall named responders

Telemetry gates (annotated signals to watch, and interpretation notes):
- Request latency p50/p95/p99 (by route): p50 shift is expected; p95/p99 regression triggers immediate rollback if >20% increase.
- Error budget burn rate: watch 15-minute burn windows; if burn >5x baseline then pause rollout.
- CPU / GPU utilization per host: rapid sustained >90% on serving nodes -> risk of queueing, consider throttling batching or revert.
- Queue latency (inference queue depth): steady increases indicate batching misconfiguration or upstream spike.
- KV cache hit ratio: expected to improve after warmup; if drops, suspect cache eviction mismatch or wrong model version getting served.
- Fault injection signals: none intentionally during rollout; any spike from chaos tools must be correlated and reported.
- Observed customer-facing rate-limited responses or 503s per region: treat as high priority.

Signal annotations: what to log and tag for post-rollout analysis
- Tag all canary traffic with release_id and lane_id (e.g., release:2026-08-23-sunrise, lane:canary-1).
- Attach 'ramp-step' metadata to traces so we can slice by ramp window.
- Add custom histogram for 'kv-warmup-latency' sampled at 10% to correlate cold-paths.
- Emit 'batch-size-avg' as a metric for streaming routes to validate batching profile shifts.

Mitigation playbook (quick actions):
- If p99 latency > threshold or errors spike: immediately switch canary lane to 'drain' (stop new requests) and apply auto-rollover to previous model via smart routing fallback. Notify SRE and product owner.
- If queue depth rising: escalate to infra to increase worker replicas or scale up instance type; concurrently decrease batch window size as a hotfix.
- If KV cache hit drops by >10%: rotate cache config to previous profile and purge suspect entries, then re-warm.
- If regional saturated: move traffic to next-best region with compatibility mapping; enable degraded routing for latency-sensitive customers.

Release notes draft (short, customer-facing snippet - keep conservative):
- Title: "Low-latency routing improvements and model timeout tuning (Aug 2026)"
- Summary: "Today we rolled out a targeted routing and model-serving tweak aimed at reducing tail latency for short-text generation routes. This change improves p95 response times for most workloads and includes safety fallbacks to preserve availability."
- Technical details (brief): "Adjusted routing thresholds for short-text routes, tuned model timeout and batching windows, and enabled regional warmup ramps. No API contract changes."
- Impact: "No breaking changes. Customers may see lower 95th percentile latency for short responses. If you see increased errors, contact support with the request id and timestamp."
- Rollback link: internal:REL-1023 (runbook)

Communication plan:
- T-24h: Post internal announcement with links to dashboard and runbook (channel: #release-ops)
- T0: Short status update in #release-ops and #sre with green/yellow/red tag and link to snapshot tables
- T+3h: Publish customer-facing release note if rollout completes successfully; otherwise postpone publication and file incident follow-up.

Post-rollout capture list (for 72h):
- Collect all span traces tagged release_id=* and generate p99 diff charts by region and route
- Export batch-size distribution and KV hit-rate deltas to the evaluation notebook
- Ask product to pull a small set of in-app prompts for quality eval of model behavior (pre-defined prompt set)
- Create a short retrospective doc with timeline, decisions, minutes from the release call

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Should warmup reserve be 30% or 40% for GPU-backed lanes? (Priya to validate cost vs safety)
- Decide on default canary length: 20m vs 30m. Longer improves signal but delays full rollout.
- Validate current observability sample rates are sufficient to detect p99 regressions for low-volume routes.

Notes to oncall:
- If you need to escalate, page Diego (primary) then Jonah (backup).
- Use rollback script in infra/tools/release-fallback and note the exact timestamp in the release log.
- Annotate any manual mitigations in the release audit so we can avoid repeating the same steps.

Appendix: quick checklist for the morning of rollout (T-4h to T+3h):
- [ ] Confirm quiet window requested and accepted
- [ ] Snapshot dashboards saved and link posted
- [ ] Canary lanes ready and traffic tag config applied
- [ ] Observability short-lived alerts created and tested
- [ ] Rollback contacts paged and on-standby
- [ ] Release notes draft locked and assigned to comms if publishing

End of draft.

Notes: this doc is intentionally compact; use it as the canonical 'sunrise rollout' pattern for small-scope performance tweaks. I'll iterate with the SRE and Observability owners to add any missing signals or automation hooks.
